headline: Former US Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin warns that the AI investment boom carries financial and social risks.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 1: remarks on Tue 6 Oct, before the 7 Oct window (stale).
importance_line: His warning on circular AI commitments and white-collar job losses affects investors and workers, but it is one former official's view, and he still calls the US the best place to invest.
summary: Bloomberg reports that Robert Rubin, the former US Treasury secretary and former Goldman Sachs co-chairman, warned at the Greenwich Economic Forum on Tuesday, 6 Oct 2026, that the AI investment boom carries financial and social risks that markets may not be fully pricing. He pointed to 'circularity risk', the overlap of commitments between suppliers, customers and investors, and said AI could hit knowledge workers such as lawyers and accountants very hard.
notes: Stale: event Tue 6 Oct, before 7 Oct; the summary gives the date. Text read on a Yahoo Finance copy of the Bloomberg article (Bloomberg page blocked). Source is Bloomberg.
